newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: U.N. envoy heads for talks with Dostum.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy heads for talks with Dostum.

text.p: U.N. special envoy for Afghanistan Norbert Holl headed on Sunday for talks with northern Uzbek militia leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum, whose forces were battling Taleban soldiers north of Kabul.
Holl's plane stopped at the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif, but then flew on towards Shibergan airbase to the west, where he was due to meet Dostum, U.N. sources said.
It was not immediately clear if the U.N. envoy also planned to visit Taleban headquarters in the southern city of Kandahar before returning to Islamabad.
Holl has been shuttling between Mazar-i-Sharif, Kabul and Kandahar in a so-far fruitless effort to arrange a ceasefire between the Taleban and a Dostum-led opposition alliance.

Warplanes apparently belonging to the northern alliance swept over Kabul twice overnight and again early on Sunday, dropping bombs on the airport and setting off furious barrages of anti-aircaft fire, witnesses in the Afghan capital said.
The air raids were the first on Kabul since the purist Islamic Taleban took the capital a month ago.
It was not known whether the aircraft belonged to Dostum or ousted government military commander Ahmad Shah Masood.
The two allied formally two weeks ago after two years of bitter estrangement and Dostum sent tanks, artillery and men to Masood's front line on the plain north of Kabul.
Anti-Taleban forces launched an attack on a strategic pass leading to Kabul on Sunday using rockets, artillery and planes.
"We are very busy now," General Abdul Rauf Begi, Dostum's front-line commander, told reporters there.
Begi, a Russian map spread out before him, directed shells and rockets onto Taleban positions in the barren hills below the De Sabz pass, 30 km (19 miles) north of Kabul.
One of Masood's commanders, Sayid Akbar, said two planes belonging to Dostum bombed Taleban positions on the hill early on Sunday morning.
He said the attack began at 6.00 a.m (0130 GMT) and there appeared to be little or no return fire from the Taleban.
